questions.q: When does HIPAA become relevant to a ServiceNow implementation?
options: The moment the instance stores or processes protected health information, such as tickets referencing patient-related systems or data
Only if the organization is physically headquartered in a specific U.S. state
Only for organizations with more than 10,000 ServiceNow users
HIPAA applies automatically to every ServiceNow instance regardless of the data it holds
questions.explain: HIPAA is relevant specifically when protected health information is involved, not as a blanket rule applying to every instance.

questions.q: What is the single most important, honest distinction this lesson makes about ServiceNow and compliance?
options: The platform provides capabilities that help meet compliance frameworks, but actual compliance depends on the customer configuring, operating, and evidencing those capabilities correctly
ServiceNow automatically certifies every customer instance as compliant with SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR, and PCI-DSS
Compliance frameworks don't actually apply to SaaS platforms like ServiceNow
Only the ServiceNow vendor, never the customer, bears any responsibility for compliance outcomes
questions.explain: This is the shared-responsibility framing: capability exists on the platform, but compliance is achieved through correct customer-side configuration and operation.

questions.q: Which of this course's capabilities does GDPR's data-subject rights (like erasure and access requests) most directly depend on?
options: The attachment and export controls from Chapter 4, configured deliberately so a specific person's data can actually be located and handled
Multi-factor authentication alone, with no dependency on export or attachment controls
The security_admin role, which GDPR requires to be permanently active
Nothing in this course relates to GDPR in any way
questions.explain: Locating, exporting, and (where legitimate) erasing a specific person's data depends on the attachment and export controls being configured deliberately, not loosely.

questions.q: Why is 'we use ServiceNow' never by itself a valid answer to a compliance question?
options: Because using a capable platform doesn't guarantee it was configured, applied to the right data, and operated correctly — the same way owning a bank vault doesn't guarantee sound financial controls
Because ServiceNow has no security-relevant features at all
Because compliance frameworks only apply to custom-built software, never to SaaS platforms
Because every ServiceNow instance is automatically non-compliant by default
questions.explain: The platform is a real, strong tool, but whether it's actually used correctly determines whether the underlying compliance control objective is met — that's the customer's work.

questions.q: How does PCI-DSS's requirement to restrict and log access to cardholder data map onto this course's capabilities?
options: It depends on a combination of field-level security, data masking, and selective audit logging being configured together for the specific fields holding card data
It is satisfied automatically the instant encryption at rest is enabled, with no other configuration needed
PCI-DSS has no real connection to any ServiceNow platform capability
It only requires enabling SSO, independent of any ACL or audit configuration
questions.explain: No single feature satisfies PCI-DSS in isolation — it depends on several capabilities (field security, masking, audit logging) working together on the specific data that matters.
